frequency_question: How often do bilateral water treaty renewals achieve formal signature within the designated pre-expiration window when observable precursor signals are mixed?
membership_rule: Includes formal bilateral treaties governing shared river basins or water resources where an existing treaty reached a sunset clause or fixed expiration date, requiring a successor agreement.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty implementation and permanent commission continuations

provenance_note: claimed 5 hits but 7 of 7 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases; rate of 100% from only 7 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 7 named cases; believed roughly 10 major comparable transboundary water treaty renewals globally in this class.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller municipal or sub-national basin accords lacking formal state-level treaty sunset provisions.
skeleton: Historical instances of major transboundary water treaty renewals or renegotiations over a 50-year horizon, categorized by whether advance technical committee precursors were fully visible 90 days out.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 7 comparable major renewals where technical precursors were partially visible yields approximately a 71 percent base rate.
validity_reason: Bilateral treaty-making norms and hydrological interdependence frameworks evolve slowly over multi-decade horizons.
